scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-02.statement: Tariff change log has zero records.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August; need AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix underlying billing errors.

H-AMI-READ-GAP.statement: Delayed or missing AMI register reads cause estimation substitution, leading to incorrect bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Contracted manual meter reads are not uploaded or are incomplete, causing estimation and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced errors in bill calculation.

H-ESTIMATION-LOGIC-FAULT.statement: The estimate substitution algorithm is faulty, producing systematic over/under-billing when reads are missing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows dispute ticket volumes of 610 in June, 590 in July, 1180 in August, and 1260 in September 2026, indicating that volumes in August and September are roughly double those of the prior two months, confirming a surge since August.
The tariff change log contains zero records, indicating no recent tariff changes that could affect billing.

The observation shows disputed bills for both estimated (1240) and actual (1785) reads, with more disputes tied to actual reads, indicating that billing errors are not limited to estimation substitution and suggest broader issues affecting all bill types.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual meter read collection is incomplete and may be contributing to estimation and disputes.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field operations manager reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

The observation shows dispute ticket response times are within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs SLA 3.0 days) despite a high ticket count of 2440, indicating that response speed is not a primary problem even though dispute volume is elevated.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL asserts that no tariff changes have occurred this year, indicating tariff-related causes for the dispute surge are unlikely.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager, aligning with the existing dispatch approval requirement.
